title: The Kazi Abu Yusuf

full_text:
Abu Yusuf, the supreme Chief Justice of Baghdad during the reign of Harun al-Rashid, was celebrated as the greatest jurist of his age, possessing an incomparable ability to untangle the most knotted disputes through keen intellect, encyclopedic knowledge of the law, and profound common sense.

One morning, two merchants appeared before his bench. The first merchant claimed that he had left a sealed jar of pure olive oil in the care of his neighbor five years ago before departing on a long journey to India. Upon his return, the neighbor returned the jar, but the merchant discovered that beneath a layer of oil at the top, the jar was filled with copper slugs instead of the thousand gold dinars he had secretly concealed within!

The neighbor indignantly denied the charge, swearing that he had never opened the jar, pointing to the original wax seal which remained intact.

The court was perplexed: how could gold turn to copper under an unbroken seal?

Abu Yusuf examined the jar closely. He summoned three expert oil-merchants of Baghdad and asked them to taste the oil floating at the top of the vessel.

The experts tasted the oil and declared unanimously: 'This oil is fresh, harvested from the olives of this very season; it cannot be more than two months old.'

Abu Yusuf turned his piercing gaze upon the neighbor: 'You swore by your honor that you never opened the jar during the five years of your friend’s absence! How then could oil harvested two months ago find its way beneath a seal five years old?'

Trapped by his own contradiction, the dishonest neighbor fell to his knees and confessed that he had broken the seal, stolen the gold, filled the jar with copper and fresh oil, and resealed it with counterfeit wax.

Abu Yusuf compelled the thief to return the thousand gold dinars, fined him heavily for his perjury, and restored the innocent merchant’s fortune, proving that true justice examines the evidence of nature rather than the empty oaths of liars.
moral: True legal wisdom combines strict justice with humane understanding and profound equity.

Believing rumors and flattery without proof
